$comment: One term, one Arabic word, everywhere. This file is the disagreement-preventer for the whole /ar/ tree: a reviewer checks the glossary first, and any page that uses a synonym for a term listed here is a bug, not a style choice. It is content, not configuration — no generator reads it, and nothing is built from it.
reviewedNote: ARABIC REVIEW REQUIRED. Every entry below was written by an AI and has never been checked by a native speaker. The glossary is the cheapest place to start a review: correcting one line here fixes every page that follows it.
register: Simple fusha. Imperative where the interface instructs (اضغط صورتك، اختر صيغة), declarative where the page explains. Not formal MSA (no «قم بضغط», no «يرجى التكرم»), not dialect. Second person masculine singular as the neutral default, and «أنت» is written only where the sentence is ungrammatical without it.
directionality: Numerals stay Western (0-9). Units stay Latin and follow the number (100 KB، 1080 px). A Latin token inside Arabic text is wrapped in unicode-bidi isolation by the stylesheet, not by this file.

image.note: Plural: صور. A photographic picture specifically; use «رسم» for a drawing.

photo.note: Deliberately the same word as image. English distinguishes them; Arabic does not need to, and two words for one thing is the synonym drift this file exists to stop.

format.note: The container (JPEG، WebP). The format *names* stay Latin and are never transliterated.

quality.note: Both the encoder setting and the visual property — Arabic uses one word for both, which is why the UI always shows the number beside it.

download.note: A file leaving the browser to disk. Never «حفظ».

upload.note: Use ONLY where English says upload, and only about the thing the site does not do. Never reuse it for drag-and-drop — see the drop entry.

save.note: Browser-stored preferences only (the theme setting, a keyboard shortcut). A file the visitor takes away is «تحميل».

drop.note: CHANGED FROM THE BRIEF. The brief suggested «ارفع» outside the drag-and-drop context. Rejected: «رفع» is already the gloss for upload, and this site's entire promise is that nothing is uploaded — the UI would say "lift/upload" exactly where it promises not to. «أفلت» (let go) matches the shipped copy «اسحب وأفلتها».

drag and drop.note: Already in shipped Arabic; kept verbatim so existing pages do not need rewriting.

drop zone.note: Follows the drop entry, not «منطقة الإسقاط».

free.note: Free as in no charge. Not «حر» — nothing here is about liberty.

private.note: For "your files stay private". The policy page is «الخصوصية» — see the privacy entry. Do not swap them.

privacy.note: The policy and the concept. «خاص» is the adjective.

batch.note: Several files through one run. "A batch" is «دفعة», "in one go" is «دفعة واحدة».

preset.note: A named saved setting, and also a develop-style look. English uses "preset" and "style" for two different things; Arabic uses «نمط» for both, which the UI survives because the value is always shown.

slider.note: A control you drag. Shipped Arabic: «شريط الشدة».

aspect ratio.note: Shipped Arabic: «نسبة العرض إلى الارتفاع». Shorter is used in labels; the long form is acceptable in prose.

background.note: Both the image layer and the color behind it.

target size.note: CHANGED FROM THE BRIEF — the brief had no entry for this, and it is the compress tool's central idea. «الحجم المطلوب» is the rejected alternative; one of the two had to win, and «المستهدف» matches the existing shipped copy.

pixel.note: CLARIFIED FROM THE BRIEF. The brief keeps px English, but shipped Arabic already says «بعرض 160 بكسل». The rule that reconciles them: `px` in numeric readouts (1080 × 1080 px), «بكسل» in prose. Both spellings now have exactly one home.

page size.note: PDF page size. «مقاس» for a physical sheet, «الحجم» for a file — the two are not interchangeable.

order.note: The sequence of pages in a PDF.

thumbnail.note: Shipped Arabic: «صور مصغّرة». Kept, including the shadda.

cookie.note: Plural: ملفات تعريف الارتباط. The long standard form; «الكوكيز» is rejected as transliteration.

worker thread.note: Shipped Arabic: «مسار خلفي داخل التبويب نفسه». Web Worker itself stays Latin.

jurisdiction.note: Used only on the terms page, where the marker is deliberately left unresolved.
